skeleton: round beetle standing in three-quarter view facing left: root on the ground under the body; body (collar and underside) with a belly bone carrying its art; the shell (near wing case) hinged at its front on the body, with the far wing case behind it, both lifting to fly; two clear wings under the shell (shown when it opens); big head at the front-left with a face carrying eyes, brows and mouth; antennaL/antennaR on the head; six legs — legL1–3 the near front, middle and back legs in front of the body, legR1–3 the far ones behind it, shaded; a mud ball prop for roll-ball.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a friendly round beetle character, seen in three-quarter view facing left. Draw this exact beetle as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the head: the big round green head, turned to the left as in image 1, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth — keep the two rosy cheeks; no antennae.
2. the body: the beetle's body under its shell, without head, shell or legs: the dark green collar behind the head and the pale yellow-green segmented underside below the shell, as in image 1, drawn whole as one rounded oval, including what the head and the shell normally cover.
3. the shell, closed: the big glossy domed wing cases, green shading to bronze, with their shine, closed, as in image 1, alone.
4. the far half of the shell: the other wing case of the same glossy green-and-bronze shell, a narrower dome, drawn whole on its own (in image 1 it is hidden behind the near one).
5. the shell gleaming: the same closed shell as part 3, with one bright soft white shine sweeping across its glossy dome (a reflection on the shell, no stars, no sparkles).
6. the left antenna (the one on the left in image 1): a thin brown curved stalk with its round green tip, its root end a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
7. the right antenna (the one on the right in image 1): a thin brown curved stalk with its round green tip, its root end a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
8. the near flying wing: a thin clear veined beetle wing, long and spread out, the faintest pale green tint and a thin brown outline, its root end a smooth rounded edge.
9. the far flying wing: the same clear veined wing for the other side, a little smaller.
10. the near front leg (the leftmost leg in image 1, under the head): green and bronze, two segments, with its little brown foot, drawn whole from the top of the thigh, its top a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
11. the near middle leg (the big leg in the middle in image 1): drawn whole from the top of the thigh with its little brown foot, its top a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
12. the near back leg (the second big leg from the right in image 1): drawn whole from the top of the thigh with its little brown foot, its top a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
13. the far front leg (the small leg behind, just right of the near front leg in image 1): drawn whole from the top of the thigh with its little brown foot, its top a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
14. the far back leg (the rightmost leg in image 1): drawn whole from the top of the thigh with its little brown foot, its top a smooth rounded edge with no line across it.
15. a little round ball of brown mud, about as big as the beetle's head is tall, smooth and soft-looking.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body, the shell or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge with no line across it. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a friendly round beetle character; image 2 shows the same beetle cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the beetle's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the beetle in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching.
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye on the left in image 1), each with its dark iris looking to the left as in image 1:
1. the far eye as it is in image 1: a tall oval dark brown eye with white on its right side and a white sparkle.
2. the same far eye wide open and surprised: a little bigger and rounder, a warm brown iris with its white sparkle.
3. the same far eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few small lashes.
4. the same far eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
5. the same far eye sad: open, the brown eye looking down, a soft shine along the bottom, no lid slanting.
6. the same far eye crying: gently squeezed shut, a soft downward-curving line (a sad closed eye, not a smile), and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye on the right in image 1), each with its dark iris looking to the left as in image 1:
7. the near eye as it is in image 1: a big oval dark brown eye with white on its right side and a white sparkle.
8. the same near eye wide open and surprised: a little bigger and rounder, a warm brown iris with its white sparkle.
9. the same near eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few small lashes.
10. the same near eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
11. the same near eye sad: open, the brown eye looking down, a soft shine along the bottom, no lid slanting.
12. the same near eye crying: gently squeezed shut, a soft downward-curving line, and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
Row 3, the brows and mouths:
13. the far eye's thin dark brown brow arc as in image 1; 14. the near eye's thin dark brown brow arc as in image 1; 15. the far brow sad, tilted up towards the middle of the face; 16. the near brow sad, tilted up towards the middle of the face.
17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a wide gentle dark brown smile.
18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh: smooth and pink inside with a little pink tongue, no teeth at all.
19. the mouth open in a small round 'o', pink inside, no teeth.
20. the mouth in a small sad frown.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the beetle scuttles along to the left on its six busy little legs, then stops.
the beetle lifts its shiny wing cases and flies along to the left on its thin clear wings, then lands and folds them away.
the beetle shakes its head no.
the beetle looks one way, then the other, then back.
the beetle wiggles its two little antennae, one way and the other, feeling the air.
the beetle laughs and laughs, bouncing on its little legs with giggles.
the beetle does a happy little dance, swaying from side to side and tapping its little legs.
the beetle cries, head down and antennae drooping, its little body shaking with sobs.
the beetle gives a big yawn, closes its eyes and dozes off, its antennae drooping, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: the beetle fast asleep, eyes shut, its head and antennae drooping

animations.description: the beetle lifts one little front leg and waves hello.
the beetle pulls its legs in under its shell and sits down flat and still, peeking about, then pops back up on its legs.

pause.shows: the beetle tucked down flat under its shiny shell, legs pulled in, keeping very still

animations.description: the beetle pats together a little ball of mud and rolls it along with its back legs, push, push, as some beetles really do, then smiles as it rolls away.
the beetle puffs up proudly and its shiny shell gleams in the light.
the beetle lifts its shiny wing cases and spreads the two thin clear wings folded underneath, flutters them without flying off, then folds them all away.

pause.shows: the beetle with its shiny wing cases lifted and its two thin clear wings spread out
